atAGlance: Bánh xèo is a crisp turmeric-rice pancake eaten with your hands: tear, wrap with herbs and rice paper or lettuce, then dip.
whatItIs: Bánh xèo is a sizzling turmeric-rice pancake folded around pork, shrimp, bean sprouts, and herbs. The point is the eating ritual, not a fork-and-knife pancake: tear a piece, wrap it, add herbs, dip lightly.
howToEnjoy: Build one bite at a time. Keep the wrapper small enough to hold, add herbs for freshness, and dip instead of soaking so the crisp edge still matters.
howLocalsOrder: Order bánh xèo expecting a shared wrap-and-dip plate. Ask for more rice paper or more herbs if the table needs them, and ask for no chili before the dip gets too spicy.
worthKnowing: Styles change by region across Vietnam, but the useful traveler pattern stays the same: crisp pancake, fresh herbs, wrapper, and fish-sauce dip working together in one bite.
goodToKnow: Fresh herbs and wrappers are part of the dish. Extra rice paper or herbs is a normal ask when the table is sharing.
travelerCaution: Often contains shrimp or pork; ask first if that matters.
